message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.16","text":"That each person’s soul, in accordance with its preconceptions, depicts forms of demons, and that the so-called gods do not appear, is clear from the fact that they do not appear to Jews. But someone will say, “How, then, do they deliver oracles foretelling the future?” This too is false. Yet grant that it is true: does that therefore make such a thing a god? For something is not a god merely because it foretells the future. Python mediums also foretell the future, but when adjured by us as demons, they are driven away. But someone will say, “They prescribe treatments for some people.” That is false. Yet grant that this is so: does that therefore make such a thing a god? Physicians also heal many people, and they are not gods. “But,” someone says, “physicians do not invariably heal those for whom they care, whereas these both deliver an oracle and heal.” Demons, however, know the remedies actually suited to each particular ailment. Consequently, they are knowledgeable physicians capable of healing—even these ailments that human beings are capable of healing—but they are also divinatory beings and know when each ailment is cured spontaneously; at that time they prescribe the treatments, so that they may claim the credit for themselves.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὰς προλήψεις","chosen":"in accordance with its preconceptions","rationale":"πρός with the accusative indicates correspondence to each soul’s prior conceptions, according to which it depicts the demonic forms."},{"source_quote":"πύθωνες","chosen":"Python mediums","rationale":"The term denotes persons or agencies associated with a Python spirit and divination. Alternatives include “Python spirits” and “those possessed by Python.”"},{"source_quote":"δεδόσθω δὲ ἀλήθειαν εἶναι, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν","chosen":"Yet grant that it is true: does that therefore make such a thing a god?","rationale":"Although the last clause is printed as a statement, the immediately following denial supports taking it as a rhetorical question: even genuine prediction would not establish divinity."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων ἰαθῆναι δυνάμενα","chosen":"even these ailments that human beings are capable of healing","rationale":"The neuter ταῦτα is understood as referring to the ailments under discussion and emphasizes that they also fall within the reach of human medicine."},{"source_quote":"καὶ εἰδότα πότε ἕκαστον ἐξ αὐτομάτου θεραπεύεται","chosen":"and know when each ailment is cured spontaneously","rationale":"The neuter ἕκαστον most naturally resumes the earlier ἕκαστον πάθος, “each ailment.” A patient-focused alternative, “when each person recovers spontaneously,” is contextually possible but less directly reflects the grammatical gender and antecedent."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιγράψωσιν","chosen":"so that they may claim the credit for themselves","rationale":"Literally, they seek to “inscribe” themselves upon the cure, idiomatically attaching their own name or credit to it."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μαντικὰ ὄντα καὶ εἰδότα","issue":"The printed text shifts to neuter plural participial forms after the masculine subjects οἱ δαίμονες and ἰατροὶ ... δυνάμενοι. This may be an anacoluthon or may reflect an implicit neuter referent such as δαιμόνια. The translation follows the demons as the continuing semantic subject, but that interpretation remains provisional.","proposed_reading":"μαντικοὶ ὄντες καὶ εἰδότες","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.17","text":"For why do they announce healings by oracle only after a long time? Why, if they can do everything, do they not bring about healing without an offering? Why do they prescribe treatments for some who pray, but sometimes deliver no oracle to others who are even more closely connected with them? It is in this way: whenever a spontaneous recovery is about to occur, they make a promise so that they may claim the credit for themselves. Others fell ill and prayed, and when they recovered spontaneously, they credited those whom they had invoked and made votive offerings. Those who died after prayer, however, cannot dedicate their failures. Yet if the relatives of the dead, or some from among them, had jointly investigated the failures, you would have found the failures more numerous than the successes. But no one already prepossessed in their favor wants to expose the case against them, being ashamed or afraid. On the contrary, they join in concealing their well-attested absurdities.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἄνευ τοῦ προσφέρειν τι","chosen":"without an offering","rationale":"The substantivized infinitive means presenting something, naturally an offering in this cultic context. The more literal alternative is “without presenting anything.”"},{"source_quote":"οἰκειοτέροις οὖσιν","chosen":"who are even more closely connected with them","rationale":"The comparative describes a closer relationship or affiliation, though whether familial, cultic, or generally intimate is not specified."},{"source_quote":"οἱ μέντοι γε μετὰ εὐχὴν διαφωνήσαντες","chosen":"Those who died after prayer, however","rationale":"διαφωνέω ordinarily denotes disagreement, discrepancy, or an outcome contrary to expectation, so a broader rendering would be “those whose cases turned out otherwise after prayer.” The following reference to “the relatives of the dead” strongly supports understanding it here as a euphemistic reference to those whose failed treatment ended in death."},{"source_quote":"πλὴν εἰ οἱ συγγενεῖς τῶν τεθνεώτων ἢ ἐξ αὐτῶν τινὲς συνεζήτησαν τὰς ἀποτυχίας, πλείονας ἂν εὑρήκειτε τὰς ἀποτυχίας τῶν ἐπιτευγμάτων","chosen":"Yet if the relatives of the dead, or some from among them, had jointly investigated the failures, you would have found the failures more numerous than the successes","rationale":"The aorist indicative in the condition and the pluperfect with ἄν in the result form a retrospective contrary-to-fact construction. The referent of ἐξ αὐτῶν remains open; it may indicate some among the unsuccessful supplicants or among a broader previously mentioned group."},{"source_quote":"συνεζήτησαν τὰς ἀποτυχίας","chosen":"had jointly investigated the failures","rationale":"The verb can mean jointly examine, investigate, or discuss. “Had compiled the failures” is possible in view of the subsequent numerical comparison, but “jointly investigated” more directly preserves the verb."},{"source_quote":"προειλημμένος αὐτοῖς","chosen":"already prepossessed in their favor","rationale":"The perfect participle describes someone whose judgment has already been captured or prejudiced by them. “Previously taken in by them” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὰ πιστὰ αὐτῶν ἀτοπήματα","chosen":"their well-attested absurdities","rationale":"πιστά can mean credible, reliable, or firmly established. Here it presents the absurdities as attested evidence rather than as conduct worthy of trust."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"συνκρύβουσιν","issue":"The image-checked print has the unassimilated compound spelling συνκρύβουσιν, where συγκρύβουσιν would be the standard assimilated spelling. The printed form still yields the clear sense “conceal together” or “join in concealing.”","proposed_reading":"συγκρύβουσιν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.18","text":"How many also falsely allege oracles and healings accomplished by them, and affirm these healings with oaths? How many have hired themselves out for pay, undertaking through certain contrivances to suffer some ailment and proclaiming it as such; then, after being restored from their ailment by a counteracting influence, they say that the treatment was prescribed by oracle, so that they may credit the insensible object of worship? How many of these objects of worship were consecrated from the outset by magical art, so that each might ὑνερπολῇ and deliver oracles? And yet, after a long time, these too failed. How many now practice sorcery because they want to strengthen such things? Nevertheless, something is not a god merely because it can foretell the future or bring healing.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ταύτας βεβαιοῦνται μετὰ ὅρκων","chosen":"and affirm these healings with oaths","rationale":"The feminine plural ταύτας most directly refers to the immediately preceding θεραπείας, “healings,” rather than broadening the object to include the oracle claims."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ μισθῷ ἑαυτοὺς ἐξέδωκαν","chosen":"have hired themselves out for pay","rationale":"The expression describes placing oneself at another’s disposal in return for payment."},{"source_quote":"δι’ ἐνίων ἐπινοιῶν πάσχειν τινὰ ἀναδεξάμενοι","chosen":"undertaking through certain contrivances to suffer some ailment","rationale":"ἐπίνοιαι are devised schemes or contrivances, while ἀναδέχομαι indicates undertaking or assuming the staged affliction."},{"source_quote":"ἀντιπαθείᾳ ἀποκατασταθέντες","chosen":"after being restored from their ailment by a counteracting influence","rationale":"ἀντιπάθεια denotes an opposing or counteracting influence, possibly treatment by contraries; the source does not specify the mechanism."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα τὸ ἀναίσθητον ἐπιγράψωσιν σέβασμα","chosen":"so that they may credit the insensible object of worship","rationale":"ἐπιγράφω concerns attaching a name or credit, while the object of worship is characterized as lacking perception or sensation."},{"source_quote":"πόσα δὲ αὐτῶν","chosen":"How many of these objects of worship","rationale":"The neuter plural most naturally refers to the insensible objects of worship just mentioned, though a broader reference to the cultic phenomena remains possible."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὅμως μακρῷ χρόνῳ καὶ ταῦτα διεφώνησεν","chosen":"And yet, after a long time, these too failed","rationale":"διαφωνέω indicates that the manufactured or promised results eventually ceased to agree with the claims and proved unsuccessful. “These too turned out otherwise” is a more literal alternative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ὑνερπολῇ καὶ χρηματίζῃ","issue":"The image-checked selected edition clearly reads ὑνερπολῇ, but the surviving form cannot be securely identified as a regular lexeme or assigned a defensible English meaning in this purpose clause. It remains untranslated in the text rather than being silently corrected. The conjecture ὑπερπολῇ might suggest a sense such as “gain ascendancy” or “flourish,” but it does not establish the meaning of the supplied reading and has not been substituted for it.","proposed_reading":"ἵνα ὑπερπολῇ καὶ χρηματίζῃ","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"9.19","text":"For God can do everything. He is good and just, showing patience toward everyone now, so that those who are willing, after regretting the evil deeds they committed and living accordingly, may, on the day when everything is judged, receive what they deserve. Therefore begin now, obeying God, the cause of good knowledge, to oppose your evil desires and thoughts, so that you may recover for yourselves the original saving religion handed down to humanity. In this way good things will immediately spring up for you; once you have received them, you will thereafter leave behind your experience of evils. But give thanks to the one who gave them, reigning forever with the King of Peace over the inexpressible good things. At present, after washing yourselves in an ever-flowing river or spring, or indeed even in the sea, with the thrice-blessed invocation, you will not only be able to drive away the spirits lurking in your innermost recesses, but—if you yourselves no longer sin and believe God without wavering—you will drive out other people’s evil spirits and fierce demons, together with their dreadful afflictions. Sometimes, however, they will flee when you merely yield. For they recognize those who have given themselves to God, and therefore, showing them honor, they flee in fear. Just as yesterday you saw how, when after the discourse I undertook to pray for those who were suffering, the afflictions themselves cried aloud out of respect for the religion, unable to endure for even a short time.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μεταμεληθέντες","chosen":"after regretting","rationale":"The verb denotes regret or a changed concern regarding the evils committed. It is kept distinct from the μετανοέω terminology governed by the reorientation policy."},{"source_quote":"καὶ πολιτευσάμενοι","chosen":"and living accordingly","rationale":"πολιτεύομαι concerns conducting one’s life. “Accordingly” expresses the contextual connection with regret; the more formally literal alternative is “and having conducted their lives.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀγαθῆς γνώσεως αἰτίᾳ θεῷ πειθόμενοι","chosen":"obeying God, the cause of good knowledge","rationale":"The dative αἰτίᾳ is taken in apposition to θεῷ, identifying God as the cause of good knowledge. Other possible attachments are “because of good knowledge, obeying God” and “for the sake of good knowledge, obeying God.”"},{"source_quote":"τὴν πρώτην τῇ ἀνθρωπότητι παραδοθεῖσαν σωτήριον θρησκείαν","chosen":"the original saving religion handed down to humanity","rationale":"πρώτην characterizes the religion as first or original, while σωτήριον describes it as saving. The wording preserves the author’s historical claim without harmonization."},{"source_quote":"ἅτινα λαβόντες πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν τοῦ λοιποῦ καταλείψετε","chosen":"once you have received them, you will thereafter leave behind your experience of evils","rationale":"The chosen attachment takes ἅτινα, referring to the good things, as the object of λαβόντες and πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν as the object of καταλείψετε. A grammatically possible alternative joins λαβόντες πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν, “having experienced evils,” and takes ἅτινα as the object of καταλείψετε: “which, after experiencing evils, you will thereafter leave behind.” That alternative would make the promised good things what is abandoned and is therefore contextually difficult."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ τρισμακαρίᾳ ἐπονομασίᾳ","chosen":"with the thrice-blessed invocation","rationale":"ἐπονομασία can mean naming, designation, or invocation. In the washing context, “invocation” conveys an enacted naming formula without supplying words not quoted in the source."},{"source_quote":"οὐ μόνον τὰ ἐνδομυχοῦντα ὑμῖν πνεύματα ἀπελάσαι δυνήσεσθε, ἀλλ᾽ αὐτοὶ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ θεῷ ἀνενδοιάστως πιστεύοντες τὰ ἄλλων κακὰ πνεύματα καὶ δαιμόνια χαλεπὰ σὺν τοῖς δεινοῖς πάθεσιν ἀπελάσετε","chosen":"you will not only be able to drive away the spirits lurking in your innermost recesses, but—if you yourselves no longer sin and believe God without wavering—you will drive out other people’s evil spirits and fierce demons, together with their dreadful afflictions","rationale":"The first member explicitly expresses ability with ἀπελάσαι δυνήσεσθε, whereas the second uses the direct future ἀπελάσετε. The English therefore does not extend “be able” over the second expulsion."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἐνδομυχοῦντα ὑμῖν πνεύματα","chosen":"the spirits lurking in your innermost recesses","rationale":"ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or hiding deep within and preserves the source’s spatial image."},{"source_quote":"μόνον ἐνδόντων ὑμῶν","chosen":"when you merely yield","rationale":"The genitive absolute uses ἐνδίδωμι in the intransitive sense “yield” or “give way.” In context it may mean yielding oneself to God, as the following clause about self-dedication suggests; “when you merely consent” or “when you merely permit it” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὰ τὰ πάθη ... ἀνέκραγεν","chosen":"the afflictions themselves cried aloud","rationale":"The neuter plural subject takes a singular verb, a regular Greek construction. The personification, or identification of the afflictions with their spiritual agents, is preserved rather than explained away."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.20","text":"Therefore, do not suppose that we are unafraid of demons because we are of a different nature. For we are of the same nature as you, though not of the same religion. Consequently, being superior to you not merely by much but altogether, we do not begrudge your becoming such people; on the contrary, we counsel you to do so, knowing that all these beings, in an uncomprehending way, hold in special regard and fear those who have become closely allied with God.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡμεῖς ἄλλης φύσεως ὄντες κατὰ τοῦτο δαίμονας οὐ φοβούμεθα","chosen":"we are unafraid of demons because we are of a different nature","rationale":"The warning rejects a proposed explanation of their fearlessness, not necessarily the claim that they are unafraid: their freedom from fear comes from religion rather than a different nature."},{"source_quote":"τῆς γὰρ αὐτῆς ὑμῖν ἐσμὲν φύσεως, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ θρησκείας","chosen":"For we are of the same nature as you, though not of the same religion","rationale":"The second genitive is elliptical, contrasting shared human nature with differing religion or worship."},{"source_quote":"οὐ πολύ, ἀλλὰ τὸ πᾶν κρείττονες","chosen":"superior to you not merely by much but altogether","rationale":"The compressed expression is literally “not much, but the whole/altogether.” The rendering treats it as a rhetorical escalation beyond superiority by degree to comprehensive superiority. “Not by much, but in every respect superior” is a more formally literal but potentially contradictory-sounding alternative; no correction of the printed πολύ is warranted."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὑμᾶς τοιούτους γενέσθαι οὐ φθονοῦμεν","chosen":"we do not begrudge your becoming such people","rationale":"τοιούτους refers to becoming people of the religious standing just described, while φθονέω means begrudging or envying another’s acquisition of that standing."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς θεῷ προσοικειωθέντας","chosen":"those who have become closely allied with God","rationale":"προσοικειόω denotes being brought into close relationship or affinity. Alternatives include “those made God’s own” and “those who have drawn near to God.”"},{"source_quote":"ταῦτα πάντα ἀγνώστως προτιμᾷ καὶ φοβεῖται","chosen":"all these beings, in an uncomprehending way, hold in special regard and fear","rationale":"The neuter plural collectively refers to the demonic beings or powers under discussion and takes singular Greek verbs. ἀγνώστως may mean “unknowingly,” “without understanding,” or “in an inexplicable manner.” The chosen wording allows the beings to recognize God’s people, as stated previously, without necessarily understanding their standing or authority."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
